description: Biotechnology involves using living organisms or their cellular components to develop useful products for human welfare. Nanotechnology is an advanced scientific field dealing with the manipulation and control of matter at a microscopic scale of 1 to 100 nanometers.

sections.title: Basic Principles of Biotechnology
sections.description: The foundational techniques and processes that combine biology with technology to modify organisms at the genetic level.

key_concepts.explanation: The artificial manipulation, modification, and recombination of an organism's DNA or other nucleic acid molecules to alter its phenotype.
The scientific process of joining together DNA molecules from two different species to create a new, functional hybrid DNA.
The biological process of creating an exact, identical genetic copy of a cell, tissue, or an entire living organism.

historical_events.significance: She was the world's first mammal to be successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell.

sections.title: Major Applications of Biotechnology
sections.description: Revolutionary and highly successful implementations of biotechnological principles in agriculture and modern medicine.

key_associations.extra_info: A genetically modified (GM) pest-resistant crop that produces a natural insecticide to combat bollworms.
A biofortified crop specifically developed to combat night blindness and malnutrition in developing nations.
The first genetically engineered hormone produced using E. coli bacteria, widely used in the treatment of Diabetes.
A revolutionary gene-editing technology that allows scientists to precisely cut and modify specific DNA sequences.

sections.title: Introduction to Nanotechnology
sections.description: The study and application of materials at the atomic and molecular scale, where physical and chemical properties of matter drastically change.

key_concepts.explanation: A standard metric unit of length that is exactly equal to one-billionth of a meter (10^-9 meters).
Cylindrical nanostructures of graphene that are exceptionally strong (stronger than steel) and serve as excellent electrical conductors.
A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a 2D hexagonal lattice, widely recognized as the thinnest and strongest material known to humanity.

important_facts.fact: Renowned physicist Richard Feynman is widely considered the 'Father of Nanotechnology' due to his visionary 1959 lecture titled 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom'.
The term 'Nanotechnology' was first officially coined and defined in 1974 by the Japanese scientist Norio Taniguchi.

sections.title: Applications of Nanotechnology
sections.description: The practical utilization of nanomaterials across diverse sectors such as healthcare, advanced electronics, and environmental conservation.

key_associations.extra_info: Used to deliver powerful medicines directly to tumors or cancer cells without damaging surrounding healthy cells.
Utilized in wound bandages, modern water purifiers, and odor-resistant fabrics to effectively kill bacteria.
Artificial nano-semiconductors that emit specific colors of light, heavily used in advanced TV screens, LEDs, and solar panels.

important_facts.fact: The Government of India launched the 'Nano Mission' in 2007, under the leadership of Prof. C.N.R. Rao, to aggressively promote nanoscience research and development.
